segments.title: Who does your shop lock out?
lines: AI shoppers with different access needs try a real web shop, in a real browser.

captions.text: Let Them In sends AI shoppers into a real shop and shows who gets locked out.
Each one only gets what their need allows. Joel only has keys. Maya only hears the screen reader.
The job: pick a product, put your own email in at checkout, place the order.

segments.title: The shop
lines: OpenTelemetry Demo 3.1.0, an open source web shop.
Its frontend is not changed for the first round.

captions.text: A visit only counts when the shop's own order confirmation page loads.

segments.label: Tom, mouse, before any fix, 6x speed

captions.text: Tom is the baseline. He buys in 7 steps.

segments.label: Maya, screen reader, before any fix, 4x speed

captions.text: Maya buys in 4 steps, using only what the screen reader reads out.

segments.label: Joel, keyboard only, before any fix, 5x speed

captions.text: Joel can only use the keyboard. The Add To Cart button hides its focus outline.
Joel: "I don't see the focus outline"
He keeps opening other products instead of adding one to the cart.
Joel: "I think the Add To Cart button is focused, so I'll press it"
After 30 steps he never reached the cart.

segments.label: Kofi, slow phone, before any fix, 6x speed

captions.text: Kofi is on a slow phone. Every page takes a while.
He taps Place Order. Then the cart shows empty, with no confirmation yet.

segments.title: Before: 4 of 5 bought
lines: Kofi's confirmation shows up while he is trying to buy again.

captions.text: Kofi: "The cart is empty, so the last order did not clearly complete."
The AI reads the steps of whoever got stuck, a rule-based scan and the shop's source code.
Fix 1 gives buttons a focus outline. The shop is rebuilt from the patch and the build passes.

segments.label: Joel, keyboard only, after fix 1, 4x speed

captions.text: Same five shoppers again. Joel can see the outline now, but he is still stuck.
When he opens a product from You May Also Like, the next Tab drops him back into those cards.
A scripted keyboard check finds the same trap, with no AI involved.
Fix 2: when a product opens, the page scrolls up and focus moves to Add To Cart.

segments.label: Joel, keyboard only, after fix 2, 4x speed

captions.text: Same Joel, same rules, 30 steps at most.
Add To Cart already has focus. He presses Enter.
He tabs to the email and types his own.
Place Order. Bought in 19 steps.
Before 4 of 5. After fix 1, 4 of 5. After fix 2, 5 of 5.
Each round of five shoppers cost under 1 USD in AI calls.

segments.title: Let Them In
lines: Find who your shop locks out, fix it, and prove they got in.
